name: 99942 Apophis
scenarioDescription: Historic sub-geostationary close approach passing inside the ring of Earth communications satellites.
description: Discovered in 2004, Apophis was initially assessed at level 4 on the Torino scale. Radar observations in 2021 permanently ruled out impact for at least a century.
educationalNotes: Demonstrates gravitational keyholes, optical astrometry refinement, and radar orbital determination.

name: 101955 Bennu
scenarioDescription: Primitive carbonaceous rubble-pile surveyed and sampled by NASA OSIRIS-REx in 2020.
description: Top-shaped rubble pile with microgravity surface acceleration ~1/100,000th of Earth.
educationalNotes: Exhibits thermal Yarkovsky orbital drift altering heliocentric semi-major axes over multi-century timeframes.

name: 162173 Ryugu
scenarioDescription: Visited by JAXA Hayabusa2 spacecraft, which collected pristine sub-surface material in 2019.
description: Spin-shaped rubble-pile containing hydrated phyllosilicates and prebiotic amino acids.
educationalNotes: High porosity (~50%) demonstrates the physical structure of primordial Solar System planetesimals.

name: 65803 Didymos
scenarioDescription: Primary target of NASA’s historic DART kinetic impactor mission, which altered Dimorphos’s orbital period by 33 minutes.
description: Sub-kilometer binary asteroid system allowing precision terrestrial ground-based radar verification of kinetic deflection.
educationalNotes: Demonstrates momentum transfer enhancement factor (beta parameter) caused by ejecta recoil.

name: 16 Psyche
scenarioDescription: Enormous metallic world in the main asteroid belt targeted by NASA Psyche mission.
description: Represents the stripped core of an early differentiated protoplanet from the solar system’s first millions of years.
educationalNotes: Provides direct insights into planetary core formation inaccessible inside Earth.

name: 433 Eros
scenarioDescription: First asteroid orbited and landed upon by human spacecraft (NEAR Shoemaker in 2001).
description: Elongated peanut-shaped stony asteroid with extensive boulder fields and impact ponds.
educationalNotes: Historical benchmark for in-situ asteroid mineralogy and gamma-ray spectrometer surveys.

name: 3200 Phaethon
scenarioDescription: Parent body of the annual Geminid meteor shower. Passes closer to the Sun than any named asteroid.
description: Surface temperatures exceed 750°C at periapsis, causing intense thermal rock fracturing and sodium gas emissions.
educationalNotes: Illustrates the transitional boundary between traditional rocky asteroids and volatile cometary bodies.

name: 4179 Toutatis
scenarioDescription: Chaotically rotating contact binary asteroid surveyed by Goldstone radar and China’s Chang’e 2 probe.
description: Lobed geometry resulting from the gentle gravitational merging of two distinct bodies in early solar history.
educationalNotes: Non-principal axis rotation ("tumbling") with two independent rotational periods of 5.4 and 7.3 days.

name: SIM-2026-001 (Aero-Vector Alpha)
scenarioDescription: Illustrative close encounter passing well inside the Moon’s orbit at 0.20 Lunar Distances.
description: Demonstration scenario modeling high-cadence optical ground discovery 14 days prior to close perigee.
educationalNotes: Demonstrates rapid astrometric arc refinement and orbit uncertainty reduction during optical discovery.

name: SIM-2026-002 (Caelus Shard)
scenarioDescription: Chelyabinsk-scale boulder entering sub-lunar space with high entry inclination.
description: Simulated high-inclination flyby crossing near geostationary orbital altitudes.
educationalNotes: Highlights how small bodies (<20m) are frequently discovered only days or hours prior to periapsis.

name: SIM-2026-003 (Vulcan Sentinel)
scenarioDescription: Regional-scale synthetic asteroid exceeding the 140-meter Congressional planetary defense threshold.
description: Modeled regional-scale encounter exhibiting moderate eccentricity and significant infrared albedo contrast.
educationalNotes: Objects ≥140m are primary targets for space-based infrared survey missions like NASA NEO Surveyor.

name: SIM-2026-004 (Helios Drifter)
scenarioDescription: Slow-moving Amor-class object orbiting entirely outside Earth’s orbit, skimming outer perihelion.
description: Exterior orbital crossing where relative speed remains exceptionally low (11.3 km/s).
educationalNotes: Amor asteroids do not cross Earth’s orbit directly but can evolve into Apollo orbits via Jupiter perturbations.

name: SIM-2026-005 (Titanis Core)
scenarioDescription: Hypothetical high-density metallic fragment exhibiting radar cross-sections consistent with iron cores.
description: High kinetic energy density scenario: high density (ρ ≈ 3,500 kg/m³) paired with elevated speed (26.5 km/s).
educationalNotes: Highlights how density drastically shifts the kinetic energy output for asteroids of identical physical diameter.

name: SIM-2026-006 (Nyx Glider)
scenarioDescription: Simulated Aten-class body with an orbital period under one Earth year, crossing interior orbits.
description: Interior orbit body passing Earth’s orbital path from the sunward direction.
educationalNotes: Sunward approaches are notoriously difficult for ground optical telescopes due to daytime glare.

name: SIM-2026-007 (Zephyr Particle)
scenarioDescription: Small porous aggregate crossing within one third of the distance to the Moon.
description: Illustrative low-density flyby exhibiting significant lightcurve tumbling behavior.
educationalNotes: Illustrates lightcurve photometric analysis used to determine asteroid rotation periods and shapes.

name: SIM-2026-008 (Kronos Bastion)
scenarioDescription: Large differentiated fragment hypothesized to originate from a major collision on protoplanet 4 Vesta.
description: V-type basaltic mantle rock with high thermal inertia and pronounced pyroxene absorption bands.
educationalNotes: Spectral classification links near-Earth objects directly to parent asteroid families in the main belt.

name: SIM-2026-009 (Selene Grazing Vector)
scenarioDescription: Tunguska-scale object making an extraordinarily close non-impacting pass at 0.16 Lunar Distances.
description: Simulated sub-lunar flyby with an Earth-miss distance barely 1.5 times the geostationary orbit perimeter.
educationalNotes: Demonstrates gravitational focus: Earth’s gravitational field bends the flyby trajectory into a hyperbola.

name: SIM-2026-010 (Astraea Veil)
scenarioDescription: Benchmark 140-meter asteroid exactly straddling the statutory boundary for hazardous object cataloging.
description: Modeled rubble pile held together by microgravity cohesion, exhibiting low radar reflectivity.
educationalNotes: The 140m benchmark represents objects that would survive atmospheric entry to produce severe ground damage.

name: SIM-2026-011 (Phaethon Minor)
scenarioDescription: High-speed object with a perihelion inside Mercury’s orbit, shedding fine particulate regolith.
description: Simulated high-velocity encounter traveling at 32.4 km/s relative to Earth.
educationalNotes: High relative velocities multiply kinetic energy exponentially according to the E ∝ v² formulation.

name: SIM-2026-012 (Gaea Wanderer)
scenarioDescription: Atira-class object orbiting entirely interior to Earth’s orbit, crossing the outbound node.
description: Interior Earth-orbiting asteroid exhibiting a near-circular low-inclination path.
educationalNotes: Atira objects (Apohele) have aphelia < 0.983 AU and never venture outside Earth’s orbital distance.

name: SIM-2026-013 (Hyperion Wedge)
scenarioDescription: Significant sub-kilometer asteroid on an eccentric orbit extending to Jupiter’s inner boundary.
description: Modeled elongated body with strong gravitational resonances with the Earth-Moon barycenter.
educationalNotes: Orbital resonances with Jupiter (Kirkwood gaps) act as cosmic gravitational slingshots into NEO space.

name: SIM-2026-014 (Iris Luminary)
scenarioDescription: Volatile-rich carbonaceous object displaying strong 0.7-micron hydrated mineral features.
description: Simulated hydrated asteroid with high scientific interest for potential in-situ resource utilization.
educationalNotes: Hydrated asteroids contain up to 10% water by weight trapped in crystalline clay lattices.

name: SIM-2026-015 (Vesper Mirage)
scenarioDescription: Extremely close flyby passing within 34,800 km of Earth’s surface, skimming near geosynchronous orbit.
description: Small monolithic boulder rotating rapidly with an estimated rotation period of just 8 minutes.
educationalNotes: Fast-rotating asteroids (<2.2 hours) must be cohesive monolithic rocks rather than loose rubble piles.

name: SIM-2026-016 (Erebus Anvil)
scenarioDescription: Massive high-speed synthetic asteroid with extreme radar reflectivity and high bulk density.
description: Hypothetical massive body yielding high potential kinetic energy due to combined high mass and high speed.
educationalNotes: Radar observation during close approach allows scientists to map surface topography with meter-scale resolution.

name: SIM-2026-017 (Clotho Filament)
scenarioDescription: Exterior orbit crossing passing through the outbound Mars-Earth orbital highway.
description: Modeled Amor asteroid with stable orbital evolution across the next several centuries.
educationalNotes: Long-term n-body gravitational simulations track asteroid positions incorporating planetary perturbations.

name: SIM-2026-018 (Thalassa Reef)
scenarioDescription: Dimorphos-class rubble-pile synthetic object passing comfortably outside lunar orbit.
description: Simulated low-albedo object with an orbital period of 2.1 years, producing recurring encounters.
educationalNotes: Recurring close approaches allow international astronomers to refine the asteroid’s orbit through multiple apparitions.

name: SIM-2026-019 (Aether Spark)
scenarioDescription: Fast-moving small meteoroid passing within a quarter of the lunar distance.
description: Modeled high-iron ordinary chondrite with high compressive strength.
educationalNotes: Iron-rich chondrites have higher tensile strength than volatile rubble piles and penetrate deeper into atmospheres.

name: SIM-2026-020 (Boreas Hammer)
scenarioDescription: Large Apollo asteroid crossing Earth’s orbit during northern hemisphere spring.
description: Simulated high-mass object with complex surface mineralogy including olivine and orthopyroxene.
educationalNotes: Planetary defense deflection requires years of warning to apply subtle delta-v nudges using kinetic impactors.

name: SIM-2026-021 (Janus Vector)
scenarioDescription: Amor asteroid with slow encounter velocity and low surface gravity.
description: Modeled carbonaceous rubble body exhibiting very low escape velocity (~0.08 m/s).
educationalNotes: Spacecraft attempting to sample low-gravity asteroids must use thrusters or micro-harpoons to prevent bouncing.

name: SIM-2026-022 (Naiad Quill)
scenarioDescription: House-sized asteroid passing within roughly one third of the Earth-Moon gap.
description: Simulated tumbling chondrite with optical lightcurves indicating a prolate spheroid shape.
educationalNotes: Radar delay-Doppler imaging constructs 3D computer terrain models of passing near-Earth asteroids.

name: SIM-2026-023 (Tethys Obelisk)
scenarioDescription: Substantial near-kilometer synthetic object with widespread regional-scale impact potential.
description: Large monolithic/rubble aggregate with massive inertia and distinct rotational poles.
educationalNotes: NASA has discovered over 95% of asteroids larger than 1 km in diameter, none of which pose near-term collision risk.

name: SIM-2026-024 (Zeus Aegis)
scenarioDescription: Largest synthetic object in the demonstration catalog, passing safely at 16.1 Lunar Distances.
description: Major near-kilometer body with extensive geological diversity, craters, and gravitational facets.
educationalNotes: Demonstrates the contrast between celestial scale and miss distance: even an 850m asteroid at 16 LD is completely safe.

name: SIM-2026-025 (Pallas Shiver)
scenarioDescription: Typical medium-scale Amor asteroid exhibiting steady, predictable orbital mechanics.
description: Modeled stony asteroid with an orbital inclination of 12.4 degrees relative to the ecliptic.
educationalNotes: High orbital inclination protects Earth by limiting close approach opportunities to narrow nodal crossings.

name: SIM-2026-026 (Nemesis Spark)
scenarioDescription: Closest synthetic encounter in the dataset: skimming Earth at just 32,000 km altitude.
description: Small boulder-sized object flying inside the geostationary ring (~35,786 km altitude).
educationalNotes: Sub-geostationary flybys are rare but provide extraordinary scientific opportunities for high-resolution ground radar imaging.

name: SIM-2026-027 (Tartarus Boulder)
scenarioDescription: High-speed regional hazard synthetic object passing at 4.55 Lunar Distances.
description: Modeled cohesive rubble body with substantial regolith migration across surface gravity lows.
educationalNotes: Spacecraft deflection strategies include the Gravity Tractor, which uses the spacecraft’s own mutual mass attraction.

name: SIM-2026-028 (Ares Courier)
scenarioDescription: Amor asteroid intersecting Mars-crossing orbital lanes with minimal relative velocity.
description: Simulated low-velocity pass with steady photometric returns.
educationalNotes: Mars serves as a major gravitational gateway, perturbing main belt asteroids into near-Earth trajectories.

name: SIM-2026-029 (Chiron Wanderer)
scenarioDescription: Extremely high velocity flyby at 36.5 km/s on an eccentric path from outer solar system reservoirs.
description: Hypothetical dormant cometary nucleus with an organic-rich refractory crust masking subsurface volatiles.
educationalNotes: Extreme velocity encounters drastically compress the warning timeline and complicate intercept trajectory planning.

name: SIM-2026-030 (Eos Radiant)
scenarioDescription: Sub-lunar flyby passing at 110,000 km, exhibiting high surface albedo.
description: Modeled bright stony asteroid with an albedo of 0.24, making it readily detectable by visible optical telescopes.
educationalNotes: Optical surveys infer diameter from apparent brightness, requiring assumptions about surface albedo reflectivity.

name: SIM-2026-031 (Hydra Crest)
scenarioDescription: Sub-kilometer synthetic asteroid on an Earth-crossing trajectory with an orbital period of 1.9 years.
description: Simulated tumbling asteroid with prominent equatorial ridge caused by rotational spin-up.
educationalNotes: The YORP effect (thermal photon recoil) gradually accelerates an asteroid’s rotation, forming characteristic equatorial ridges.

name: SIM-2026-032 (Vesta Shard Beta)
scenarioDescription: Vesta family fragment flying safely outside Earth’s orbital boundary.
description: High-density igneous rock with volcanic pyroxene crystals identical to Howardite-Eucrite-Diogenite meteorites.
educationalNotes: Laboratory analysis of fallen meteorites connects terrestrial geology directly to spectroscopic asteroid surveys.

name: SIM-2026-033 (Astra Sentinel)
scenarioDescription: Potentially hazardous synthetic body crossing the ecliptic plane at 4.29 Lunar Distances.
description: Modeled contact binary with two distinct lobes resting against one another.
educationalNotes: Contact binaries comprise up to 15% of the near-Earth asteroid population, reflecting low-velocity collision histories.

name: SIM-2026-034 (Kalliope Fragment)
scenarioDescription: Dense sub-lunar flyby inside half the distance to the Moon.
description: High-density mixed metal-silicate body passing with strong ground-based radar echo signatures.
educationalNotes: Arecibo and Goldstone planetary radars have mapped hundreds of near-Earth asteroids, measuring velocity to mm/s precision.

name: SIM-2026-035 (Olympus Shard)
scenarioDescription: Major synthetic asteroid with substantial kinetic energy potential and a 2.4-year heliocentric period.
description: Modeled sub-kilometer asteroid with extensive boulders up to 30 meters resting on its regolith mantle.
educationalNotes: Boulders on asteroid surfaces demonstrate that microgravity impact gardening rearranges regolith without blowing it into space.

name: SIM-2026-036 (Hesperia Wisp)
scenarioDescription: Small boulder passing through Earth’s gravitational sphere of influence at 0.135 Lunar Distances.
description: Simulated sub-lunar flyby with measurable orbit deflection caused by Earth’s gravitational attraction.
educationalNotes: Planetary gravity assists not only steer human spacecraft but also permanently reshape asteroid orbital elements.

name: SIM-2026-037 (Bellona Core)
scenarioDescription: Dense sub-kilometer synthetic target on an Apollo orbit with a perihelion inside Earth’s orbit.
description: High-density metallic-silicate asteroid showing pronounced radar albedo and low circular polarization ratio.
educationalNotes: Circular polarization ratios measured in radar astronomy reveal wavelength-scale surface roughness.

name: SIM-2026-038 (Themis Envoy)
scenarioDescription: Moderate-scale Amor asteroid exhibiting organic spectral absorption bands.
description: Porous carbonaceous object with evidence of water ice sublimation at perihelion.
educationalNotes: Main-belt comets and volatile-rich asteroids suggest water may have been delivered to primordial Earth via asteroid bombardment.

name: SIM-2026-039 (Persephone Path)
scenarioDescription: DART-scale synthetic asteroid on an Earth-crossing Apollo orbit passing at 3.88 Lunar Distances.
description: Modeled rubble pile held together by microgravity cohesion, exhibiting low thermal inertia.
educationalNotes: NASA DART proved that kinetic impactors can deflect rubble-pile asteroids without shattering them unpredictably.

name: SIM-2026-040 (Leto Fragment)
scenarioDescription: Sub-lunar flyby skimming past Earth at less than one-fifth of the distance to the Moon.
description: Small monolithic stone rotating every 14 minutes, detected via rapid-cadence survey sensors.
educationalNotes: Wide-field sky surveys detect thousands of objects per night, using automated algorithms to flag moving asteroids against background stars.

name: SIM-2026-041 (Astraea Titan)
scenarioDescription: Half-kilometer synthetic asteroid on an Earth-crossing trajectory with an orbital period of 2.2 years.
description: Simulated high-mass object with complex surface mineralogy including olivine and orthopyroxene.
educationalNotes: Planetary defense deflection requires years of warning to apply subtle delta-v nudges using kinetic impactors.

name: SIM-2026-042 (Chronos Finale)
scenarioDescription: Major synthetic encounter closing the Phase 5 observation catalog with a safe 7.15 Lunar Distance pass.
description: Comprehensive synthetic model incorporating realistic orbital uncertainties and high-precision ephemerides.
educationalNotes: Demonstrates why international planetary defense organizations prioritize early detection: distance and time provide the margin of safety.
